prompt: What do you call text comprehensively capturing all sounds, actions and events exactly as they are happening. I want something that also included also non-verbal gestures, movement, actions, environmental changes etc.
judge_reasoning: The prompt asks what you would call a highly detailed text recording sounds/actions/events as they happen, including non-verbal gestures, movement, and environmental changes. Candidate 1 correctly points to “verbatim transcript”/“detailed transcript” approaches and appropriately notes that adding non-verbal elements makes it akin to stage directions or a multimodal/detailed scene description. Candidate 2 is on the right track conceptually (“script of events”) but is less standard and spends more on illustrative content than the terminology itself. Candidate 3 includes the right general idea (verbatim transcript with stage directions/enhanced transcript) but adds many very specific historical/organizational/accuracy claims that are unlikely to be reliably verifiable, so it should be penalized for probable fabrication. Candidate 4’s term “omniscient transcript” appears invented, despite an otherwise accurate description, making it the weakest overall.
